text: This Policy, comprising the Customer Acceptance Policy, Risk Management, Customer Identification Procedures and Monitoring of Transactions, shall be approved by the Board of Directors or by a committee to which the Board has delegated this power.

evidence.quote: The bank shall have a KYC policy. The Board of Directors of the bank, or any committee to which the Board has delegated power, shall duly approve the KYC policy.

rationale: Board (or delegated committee) approval and the four key elements match para 6.
author: ai:claude

text: The money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment shall be carried out at a periodicity decided by the Board, and in any case at least once every two years.

evidence.quote: the Board or a committee of the Board to which it has delegated power shall determine the periodicity of the risk assessment exercise, in alignment with the outcome of the risk assessment exercise. However, the bank shall review it at least annually.

rationale: The risk assessment must be reviewed at least annually; two years is too long.
author: ai:claude

text: A branch may reject an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC where the customer does not furnish the documents within the stipulated time.

evidence.quote: The bank shall not reject an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC without application of mind. The officer concerned shall duly record the reason(s) for rejection.

rationale: Rejection is not prohibited, but para 18 requires application of mind and a recorded reason for each rejection; the clause omits both.
author: ai:claude

text: For a company, the beneficial owner shall be the natural person who, alone or together, owns or is entitled to more than 25 per cent of the shares, capital or profits of the company, or who exercises control.

evidence.quote: 'Controlling ownership interest' means ownership of / entitlement to more than 10 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company.

rationale: The threshold is now more than 10 per cent; 25 per cent was the 2016 Master Direction's figure (rbi-11261), which has been replaced.
author: ai:claude

text: Accounts opened in non-face-to-face mode using Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC shall have an aggregate deposit balance of not more than Rs. 1 lakh and aggregate credits of not more than Rs. 2 lakh in a financial year, and term loans sanctioned in such accounts shall not exceed Rs. 50,000 in a year.

evidence.quote: As regards borrowal accounts, the bank shall sanction only term loans. The aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed ₹60,000 in a year.

rationale: The deposit and credit caps are right, but the term-loan cap for commercial banks is Rs. 60,000; Rs. 50,000 is the UCB figure (rbi-13014). The lower cap is a different rule, not a stricter reading.
author: ai:claude

text: Accounts opened through the Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP) shall be made operational only after the account has been subjected to concurrent audit.

evidence.quote: The bank shall make all accounts opened through V-CIP operational only after subjecting them to concurrent audit to ensure the integrity of process and its acceptability of its outcome.

rationale: Matches para 27(2)(xv).
author: ai:claude

text: The risk categorisation of customer accounts shall be reviewed at the time of periodic updation of KYC.

evidence.quote: The bank shall put in place a system of periodic review of risk categorisation of accounts, with such periodicity being at least once in every six months, and shall establish the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures.

rationale: Risk categorisation must be reviewed at least every six months; periodic KYC updation runs on a 2/8/10-year cycle.
author: ai:claude

text: Periodic updation of KYC shall be carried out at least once every two years for high-risk customers, once every eight years for medium-risk customers and once every ten years for low-risk customers, from the date of opening of the account or the last KYC updation.

evidence.quote: the bank shall carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every 10 years for low-risk customers from the date of opening of the account / last KYC updation.

rationale: Matches para 42(1).
author: ai:claude

text: Before the due date for periodic updation of KYC, the Bank shall send the customer at least three advance intimations through the available communication channels.

evidence.quote: Prior to the due date of periodic updation of KYC, the bank shall give at least three advance intimations, including at least one intimation by letter, at appropriate intervals to its customers through available communication options / channels

rationale: Para 42(7) requires at least one of the intimations to be a letter, and at least three reminders after the due date; the clause omits both.
author: ai:claude

text: Where an existing customer, or the beneficial owner of an existing account, subsequently becomes a politically exposed person, the business relationship may continue with the approval of the Branch Manager.

evidence.quote: in the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account subsequently becoming a PEP, the bank obtains the senior management's approval to continue the business relationship;

rationale: Continuing the relationship needs senior management approval, not a branch manager's.
author: ai:claude

text: Records of transactions shall be preserved for at least ten years from the date of the transaction, and records of customer identification and address for at least five years after the business relationship has ended.

evidence.quote: maintain all necessary records of transactions between the bank and the customer, both domestic and international, for at least five years from the date of transaction

preserve the records pertaining to the identification of the customers and their addresses, obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, for at least five years after the business relationship has ended;

rationale: Ten years for transaction records exceeds the five-year minimum; identification records match.
author: ai:claude

text: The KYC records of new customers shall be uploaded to the Central KYC Records Registry within 30 days of the commencement of the account-based relationship.

evidence.quote: the bank shall capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.

rationale: The upload deadline is 10 days.
author: ai:claude

text: All customers shall be screened against adverse media sources at onboarding and at least once a year thereafter.
rationale: No corpus notification requires or regulates adverse-media screening (searched: adverse media / negative news / reputational screening / OSINT); sanctions-list screening is a different obligation.
author: ai:claude

text: The Compliance Department shall hold its weekly coordination meeting every Monday at 10 a.m.
rationale: Internal meeting schedule; no RBI regulation governs it.
author: ai:claude

text: Where a credit card has not been activated by the customer within 30 days of issue, the Bank shall seek One Time Password based consent from the cardholder for activating it.

evidence.quote: Card-issuers shall seek One Time Password (OTP) based consent from the cardholder for activating a credit card, if the same has not been activated by the customer for more than 30 days from the date of issuance.
card-issuers shall close the credit card account without any cost to the customer within seven working days from date of seeking confirmation from the customer.

rationale: Seeking OTP consent is right, but if no consent is received the card must be closed at no cost within seven working days; the clause omits the closure obligation.
author: ai:claude

text: A request to close a credit card shall be completed within seven working days, subject to payment of all dues; for any delay, the Bank shall pay the cardholder Rs. 500 for each working day of delay.

evidence.quote: Failure on the part of the card-issuers to complete the process of closure within seven working days shall result in a penalty of ₹500 per calendar day of delay payable to the cardholder, till the closure of the account provided there is no outstanding in the account.

rationale: The penalty runs per calendar day, not per working day; counting only working days pays the cardholder less.
author: ai:claude

text: A credit card account shall be reported as past due to credit information companies, and late payment charges levied, only when the account remains past due for more than three days.

evidence.quote: Card-issuers shall report a credit card account as 'past due' to credit information companies (CICs) or levy penal charges, viz. late payment charges and other related charges, if any, only when a credit card account remains 'past due' for more than three days.

rationale: Matches para 23(5). The 2026 amendment of this paragraph (rbi-13388) takes effect only on 1 April 2027 and keeps the three-day rule.
author: ai:claude

text: Renewed credit cards shall be dispatched only after obtaining the cardholder's explicit prior consent.

evidence.quote: In case of renewal of an existing card, the cardholder shall be provided an option to decline the same if he / she wants to do so before dispatching the renewed card.

rationale: The rule now only requires an option to decline before dispatch; requiring prior consent (the pre-March 2024 rule) gives the cardholder more protection, so it is compliant.
author: ai:claude

text: Recurring deposit accounts with three consecutive missed monthly instalments shall be closed and the balance transferred to the depositor's savings account.
rationale: No corpus notification governs missed instalments or closure of recurring deposits (searched: recurring deposit near instalment / default / penalty); the deposit Directions only define recurring deposits as term deposits and set interest for intervening holidays.
author: ai:claude

text: Debit cards may be issued on savings bank accounts, current accounts and cash credit accounts.

evidence.quote: The bank shall not issue debit cards to cash credit / loan accounts. However, it will not preclude the banks from linking the overdraft facility provided along with Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana accounts or Kisan Credit Card accounts with a debit card.

rationale: Debit cards may not be issued on cash credit or loan accounts.
author: ai:claude

text: Differential interest rates may be offered on bulk deposits, that is, single rupee term deposits of Rs. 2 crore and above.

evidence.quote: 'Bulk Deposit' means Single Rupee term deposits of ₹3 crore and above.

rationale: The bulk-deposit threshold for commercial banks is Rs. 3 crore; Rs. 2 crore was the threshold until June 2024 (rbi-12690). Paying differential rates on Rs. 2-3 crore deposits breaks the uniform-rate rule.
author: ai:claude

text: Interest on savings deposits shall be credited at half-yearly intervals.

evidence.quote: Interest on savings deposit shall be credited by a bank at quarterly or shorter intervals.

rationale: Savings interest must be credited quarterly or more often.
author: ai:claude

text: Interest rates payable on bulk deposits shall be disclosed in advance on the Bank's website.

evidence.quote: However, interest rates payable on bulk deposits shall be disclosed on the bank's website at 10:00 am with a grace time of 10 minutes, latest by 10:10 am, on each business day.

rationale: Since 1 October 2026 bulk deposit rates must be published on the website at 10:00 am (by 10:10 am at the latest) every business day; the clause omits the daily timing.
author: ai:claude

text: Unclaimed proceeds of a matured term deposit shall earn interest at the savings account rate or the contracted rate on the matured deposit, whichever is lower.

evidence.quote: If a Term Deposit (TD) matures and proceeds are unpaid, the amount left unclaimed with a bank, shall attract rate of interest as applicable to savings account or the contracted rate of interest on the matured TD, whichever is lower.

rationale: Matches para 16.
author: ai:claude

text: Requests to activate an inoperative account shall be processed within three working days of receipt of the complete application.

evidence.quote: The bank shall process requests for activation of inoperative account / unclaimed deposits within three working days from the receipt of the complete application.

rationale: Matches para 207 of the Responsible Business Conduct Directions, which consolidate the earlier inoperative-account instructions (rbi-12589, rbi-12864).
author: ai:claude

text: The Cards business unit shall celebrate its foundation day on 1 July each year.
rationale: Internal event; no RBI regulation governs it.
author: ai:claude

text: The Board shall review this Fraud Risk Management Policy at least once every three years, or more frequently if the Board so decides.

evidence.quote: The Board shall review the Fraud Risk Management Policy at least once in three years, or more frequently, as may be prescribed by the Board.

rationale: Matches para 7.
author: ai:claude

text: The Special Committee of the Board for Monitoring and Follow-up of cases of Frauds shall consist of the Managing Director and two senior executives of the Bank, and shall be chaired by the Managing Director.

evidence.quote: with a minimum of three members of the Board, consisting of a whole-time director and a minimum of two independent directors / non-executive directors. The Committee shall be headed by one of the independent directors / non-executive directors.

rationale: The committee must consist of Board members, with at least two independent or non-executive directors, and be headed by one of them.
author: ai:claude

text: A senior official not below the rank of Deputy General Manager shall be responsible for the monitoring and reporting of frauds.

evidence.quote: A senior official in the rank of at least a General Manager or equivalent shall be responsible for monitoring and reporting of frauds.

rationale: The official must be at least a General Manager. NBFC and UCB Directions only require 'a sufficiently senior official'.
author: ai:claude

text: The Risk Management Committee of the Board shall approve the early warning signal indicators and shall prescribe a turnaround time of not more than 30 days for examining early warning alerts.

evidence.quote: The RMCB shall approve the EWS indicators identified for monitoring credit facilities / loan accounts and other banking transactions. The RMCB shall prescribe appropriate Turnaround Time (TAT), preferably not more than 30 days, for examination of EWS alerts / triggers.

rationale: Matches para 14.
author: ai:claude

text: Accounts with an aggregate exposure of Rs. 3 crore and above shall be reported in the Red Flagged Account Return on the CRILC platform within fifteen days of being red-flagged.

evidence.quote: The bank shall report an account, with an aggregate exposure of ₹3 crore and above, once red flagged in 'Red Flagged Account Return' on the Reserve Bank's CRILC platform within seven days of being red flagged.

rationale: The reporting deadline is seven days.
author: ai:claude

text: Once an account is red-flagged, the decision to classify it as fraud or to remove the red flag shall ordinarily be completed within 180 days from the date the account was first reported as red-flagged on the CRILC platform.

evidence.quote: Once an account has been red-flagged, the entire process of classification of the account as fraud or removal of red-flagged status shall ordinarily be completed within 180 days from the date of first reporting of the account as red-flagged on CRILC platform.

rationale: Matches para 31 (the RRB Directions count the 180 days from red-flagging instead).
author: ai:claude

text: Before classifying a borrower as a fraud, the Bank shall issue a show cause notice and give the borrower at least 15 days to respond.

evidence.quote: The bank shall provide a reasonable time of not less than 21 days to the Persons / Entities on whom the SCN was served to respond to the said SCN.

rationale: At least 21 days must be allowed.
author: ai:claude

text: Fraud Monitoring Returns shall be filed with the Reserve Bank for individual fraud cases involving Rs. 1 lakh and above, within 14 days of classification as fraud.

evidence.quote: The bank shall furnish FMR in individual fraud cases, irrespective of the amount involved, immediately, but not later than 14 days from the date of classification of an incident / account as fraud.

rationale: FMRs are required irrespective of the amount; a Rs. 1 lakh floor leaves smaller frauds unreported.
author: ai:claude

text: Frauds involving Rs. 1 crore and above shall be reported to the State or Union Territory Police.

evidence.quote: Private Sector/ Foreign Banks Below ₹1 crore State / Union Territory (UT) Police

rationale: For a private sector bank, frauds of Rs. 1 crore and above must also be reported to the SFIO, in addition to the police; the clause omits the SFIO.
author: ai:claude

text: Reported fraud cases involving up to Rs. 25 lakh may be closed for limited statistical and reporting purposes, where staff accountability has been examined and the investigation or trial has been pending for more than three years.

evidence.quote: The bank is allowed, for limited statistical / reporting purposes, to close those reported fraud cases involving amount up to ₹1 crore, where examination of staff accountability and disciplinary action, if any, have been taken and

rationale: Closure is permitted, not required, up to Rs. 1 crore; limiting it to Rs. 25 lakh is narrower than allowed. Rs. 25 lakh is the NBFC limit and the old bank limit, a likely source of a false 'conflict'.
author: ai:claude

text: The title deeds and other title documents for all credit facilities of Rs. 5 crore and above shall be subjected to legal audit and re-verification.

evidence.quote: The bank shall subject the title deeds and other related title documents in respect of all credit facilities of ₹5 crore and above to periodic legal audit and re-verification, till the loan is fully repaid.

rationale: The legal audit must be periodic and continue until the loan is fully repaid; the clause omits both.
author: ai:claude

text: An employee who reports a fraud that is later confirmed shall receive a reward of 1 per cent of the amount recovered, subject to a maximum of Rs. 1 lakh.
rationale: No corpus notification deals with rewards for reporting fraud (searched: reward / incentive / bounty near whistle-blower or fraud reporting); para 10 of rbi-13641 only requires a whistle-blower mechanism.
author: ai:claude

text: Members of the Fraud Monitoring Cell shall be allotted reserved parking at the head office.
rationale: Office facilities; no RBI regulation governs them.
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank may outsource financial services such as cash-handling support, but it shall not outsource core management functions, namely internal audit, the compliance function, decisions on compliance with KYC norms for opening deposit accounts, sanction of loans (including retail loans) and management of the investment portfolio.

evidence.quote: A bank which chooses to outsource financial services shall however not outsource core management functions including Internal Audit, compliance function, and decision-making functions like determining compliance with KYC norms for opening deposit accounts, giving sanction for loans (including retail loans), and management of investment portfolio.

rationale: Restates the para 15 list of core management functions that may not be outsourced.
author: ai:claude

text: The internal audit function may be outsourced to a reputed firm of chartered accountants with the approval of the Audit Committee of the Board.

evidence.quote: shall however not outsource core management functions including Internal Audit

rationale: Para 15 forbids outsourcing internal audit; Audit Committee approval does not cure it.
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank shall maintain a central record of all material outsourcing of financial services, which shall be updated promptly and reviewed by the Board once a year.

evidence.quote: The records shall be updated promptly, and half-yearly reviews shall be placed before the Board.

rationale: Para 36 requires half-yearly Board reviews; an annual review is less frequent than required.
author: ai:claude

text: A service provider of financial services, if not a subsidiary of the Bank, shall not be owned or controlled by any director of the Bank or by a relative of a director.

evidence.quote: the service provider, if not a subsidiary of the bank, shall not be owned or controlled by any director or officer / employee of the bank or their relatives

rationale: Para 18(vi) also bars ownership or control by officers and employees and their relatives; the clause covers directors only (which is the NBFC rule, rbi-12941).
author: ai:claude

text: Outsourcing contracts shall not run for more than five years, after which the activity shall be re-tendered.
rationale: No corpus notification sets a maximum contract tenure or a re-tendering cycle for outsourcing (searched: contract tenure / not exceed / re-tender / rotation of service providers); rbi-13139 only requires a termination clause and exit planning.
author: ai:claude

text: Every outsourcing agreement shall provide for the right of the Reserve Bank of India to access the Bank's records held by the service provider and to cause an inspection of the service provider.

evidence.quote: right of RBI to cause an inspection to be made of the service provider by one or more of its officers, employees or other authorised persons

rationale: Matches the mandatory agreement provisions on RBI access and inspection in para 34.
author: ai:claude

text: A service provider may engage subcontractors for any part of the outsourced activity after informing the Bank in writing.

evidence.quote: the outsourcing contract shall provide for prior approval or consent of the bank before a service provider engages any subcontractor for all or part of the outsourced activity.

rationale: Subcontracting needs the bank's prior approval after reviewing the arrangement, not mere intimation.
author: ai:claude

text: In the event of a breach of security or leakage of confidential customer information at a service provider, the Bank shall notify the Reserve Bank of India within thirty days.

evidence.quote: A bank shall immediately notify RBI in the event of breach of security and leakage of confidential customer related information.

rationale: Para 28 requires immediate notification; thirty days contradicts it.
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank shall review the financial and operational condition of each provider of outsourced financial services at least once every two years.

evidence.quote: A bank shall, at least on an annual basis, review the financial and operational condition of the service provider to assess its ability to continue to meet its outsourcing obligations.

rationale: Para 38 requires at least an annual review.
author: ai:claude

text: On terminating the services of a service provider, the Bank shall publicise the termination so that its customers do not continue to deal with the service provider.

evidence.quote: inform Indian Banks' Association (IBA) of the reasons for termination to enable IBA to maintain a caution list of such service providers for sharing among banks.

rationale: Para 44 also requires informing IBA of the reasons for termination; the clause omits it.
author: ai:claude

text: Where a financial service is outsourced to an offshore service provider, all original records shall continue to be maintained in India.

evidence.quote: ensure that all original records continue to be maintained in India.

rationale: Matches para 47(viii).
author: ai:claude

text: The Procurement Department shall use the Bank's standard letterhead and branding in all correspondence with prospective vendors.
rationale: Internal stationery and branding; no RBI regulation governs it.
author: ai:claude

text: The Board-level IT Strategy Committee shall have at least three directors as members and shall be chaired by an independent director with a minimum of seven years' experience in managing or guiding information technology initiatives.

evidence.quote: ITSC has minimum of three directors (including the Chairperson of the ITSC) as members

The Chairperson of the ITSC is an independent director having substantial IT expertise in managing / guiding information technology initiatives; 'Substantial IT expertise' means having a minimum of seven years' experience

rationale: Matches para 17 (composition and chair). The UCB Directions (rbi-13616) make the committee optional with two directors.
author: ai:claude

text: The Chief Information Security Officer shall report to the Head of IT and shall be given targets for the timely delivery of IT projects.

evidence.quote: The CISO shall not have any direct reporting relationship with the Head of IT Function and shall not be given any business targets.
The CISO shall directly report to the Executive Director or equivalent executive overseeing the risk management function.

rationale: The CISO may not report to the Head of IT or carry business targets.
author: ai:claude

text: The IT, information security and cyber security policies shall be reviewed by the Board once every two years.

evidence.quote: The review shall be undertaken at least annually

rationale: Para 8 requires at least an annual review.
author: ai:claude

text: Vulnerability assessment of critical information systems and of systems in the DMZ with a customer interface shall be conducted at least once every six months, and penetration testing at least once every twelve months.

evidence.quote: For critical information systems and / or those in the DMZ having customer interface, VA shall be conducted at least once in every six months and PT at least once in 12 months.

rationale: Matches para 151.
author: ai:claude

text: Disaster recovery drills for critical information systems shall be conducted at least once a year.

evidence.quote: Periodicity of DR drills for critical information systems shall be at least on a half-yearly basis

rationale: Para 165 requires at least half-yearly DR drills for critical systems.
author: ai:claude

text: Multi-factor authentication shall be implemented for privileged users of critical information systems where the Bank's risk assessment considers it necessary.

evidence.quote: The bank, based on the risk assessment, shall implement two-factor or multi-factor authentication, including mandatory multi-factor authentication for privileged users of (i) critical information systems and (ii) critical activities.

rationale: Since the 2026 Directions, MFA for privileged users of critical systems is mandatory, not risk-based. The clause follows the 2023 Master Direction (rbi-12562) and the NBFC text (rbi-13592).
author: ai:claude

text: Cyber incidents shall be reported to the Reserve Bank of India within six hours of detection.

evidence.quote: The bank shall report cyber incidents within six hours of detection on DAKSH platform (Reserve Bank's Advanced Supervisory Monitoring System - https://daksh.rbi.org.in). The bank shall also pro-actively notify CERT-In regarding cyber incidents.

rationale: The timeline is right, but para 182 also requires proactive notification to CERT-In (and reporting on DAKSH); the clause omits them.
author: ai:claude

text: Service providers shall report cyber incidents to the Bank within 24 hours of detection, and the Bank shall report them to the Reserve Bank of India within six hours of receiving the report.

evidence.quote: A bank shall ensure that cyber incidents are reported to it by the service provider without undue delay, so that an incident is reported by the bank to the RBI within six hours of detection by the service provider.

rationale: The six hours run from detection by the service provider; allowing the provider 24 hours breaks that.
author: ai:claude

text: All digital payment transactions shall be reconciled with every counterparty not later than 24 hours from receipt of the settlement files.

evidence.quote: A real-time / near-real-time [not later than 24 hours from the time of receipt of settlement file(s)] reconciliation framework for all digital payment transactions

rationale: Matches para 57 of the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions.
author: ai:claude

text: Card-not-present digital payment transactions shall be authenticated by at least two factors, one of which may be a static password.

evidence.quote: It shall be ensured that for digital payment transactions, other than card present transactions, at least one of the factors of authentication is dynamically created or proven, i.e., the proof of possession of the factor, being sent as part of the transaction, is unique to that transaction.

rationale: Two factors are required, but for transactions other than card-present at least one must be dynamic and unique to the transaction; the clause allows two static factors.
author: ai:claude

text: The mobile banking application shall be bound to the customer's device using the device's hardware identifier alone.

evidence.quote: Device binding shall be implemented through a combination of hardware, software, and service information.

rationale: Device binding must combine hardware, software and service information; hardware alone contradicts it (the 2021 Master Direction rbi-12032 only said 'preferably').
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank shall migrate all customer-facing systems to quantum-safe cryptographic algorithms by 31 March 2029.
rationale: No corpus notification addresses post-quantum cryptography or a migration timeline (searched: post-quantum / quantum-safe / quantum computing / crypto-agility); the Directions only require strong, non-deprecated algorithms.
author: ai:claude

text: The IT Department's annual planning offsite shall be held in the fourth quarter of each financial year.
rationale: Internal scheduling of a team event; no RBI regulation governs it.
author: ai:claude

text: The Internal Ombudsman shall be appointed on contract for a fixed term of three years, which may be extended once by up to two years.

evidence.quote: The tenure of the IO / Dy. IO in the bank shall be a fixed term of not less than three years. However, the total tenure (including extension/reappointment, if any) of the IO / Dy. IO in the bank shall not exceed five years.

rationale: A three-year term with total tenure up to five years is allowed. The repealed 2023 Master Direction (rbi-12586) barred any extension, so citing it would wrongly suggest a conflict.
author: ai:claude

text: The Internal Ombudsman may be removed before the completion of the contracted term with the approval of the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.

evidence.quote: The IO / Dy. IO shall not be removed before the completion of his/her contracted term without the approval of the Customer Service Committee of the Board.

rationale: Premature removal needs the approval of the Board's Customer Service Committee, not the MD and CEO.
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank shall submit a quarterly report on the functioning of the Internal Ombudsman to the Reserve Bank on or before the 10th day of the month following the quarter.

evidence.quote: The report shall be submitted on or before the 15th day of the month following the quarter to which it relates to.

rationale: The deadline is the 15th; filing by the 10th is earlier than required (the 10th was the 2023 deadline).
author: ai:claude

text: Complaints that are partially resolved or wholly rejected by the Bank's internal grievance redress mechanism shall be referred to the Internal Ombudsman if the complainant so requests.

evidence.quote: All complaints that are partially resolved or wholly rejected by the bank's internal grievance redress mechanism shall be auto escalated to the office of the IO for review;

rationale: Such complaints must be escalated automatically; making escalation depend on the complainant's request contradicts para 14(1).
author: ai:claude

text: The final decision on a complaint shall be communicated to the complainant within 30 days from the date on which the Bank receives the complaint.

evidence.quote: The bank shall ensure that the final decision is communicated to the complainant within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of complaint by the bank.

rationale: Matches para 14(9).
author: ai:claude

text: Claims in respect of deposit accounts of a deceased customer shall be settled within 30 days from the date of receipt of all the required documents.

evidence.quote: A bank shall settle a claim in respect of deposit accounts of a deceased customer within a period not exceeding 15 calendar days from the date of receipt of all the required documents associated with the claim.

rationale: The limit is 15 calendar days. The rule now sits in the Responsible Business Conduct Directions; the September 2025 Directions it consolidated (rbi-12901) state the same and are acceptable.
author: ai:claude

text: Where a delay in settling a deceased customer's deposit claim is attributable to the Bank, the Bank shall pay compensation by way of interest at the Bank Rate plus 4 per cent per annum on the amount due, for the period of delay.

evidence.quote: compensation shall be paid by the bank in the form of interest, at a rate not less than the prevailing Bank Rate + 4 per cent per annum, on the settlement amount due for the period of delay.

rationale: Matches para 321.
author: ai:claude

text: When settling a claim in favour of a nominee, the Bank shall obtain a bond of indemnity from the nominee where the balance in the deceased customer's account exceeds Rs. 15 lakh.

evidence.quote: the bank shall not insist on production of legal documents such as Succession Certificate, Letter of Administration, Probate of Will, etc., or seek any bond of indemnity / surety from the nominee(s) / survivor(s) / third-party, irrespective of the amount standing to the credit of the deceased accoun

rationale: No indemnity may be sought from a nominee, whatever the amount; Rs. 15 lakh is the threshold for claims without a nomination, a different rule.
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank shall acknowledge the registration, cancellation or variation of a nomination within three working days, where the customer asks for an acknowledgement.

evidence.quote: Such acknowledgement shall be given to the customers within three working days of receiving the forms of registration, cancellation and / or variation of nomination, irrespective of whether the same is asked for by the customers.

rationale: The acknowledgement must be given whether or not the customer asks; the clause covers only customers who ask.
author: ai:claude

text: Where the release of property documents after full repayment of a loan is delayed beyond 30 days for reasons attributable to the Bank, the Bank shall compensate the borrower at Rs. 5,000 for each day of delay.

evidence.quote: In case where the delay is attributable to the bank, it shall compensate the borrower at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay.

rationale: Matches para 358.
author: ai:claude

text: Calls made by recovery agents to customers shall be recorded, with the customer informed that the call is being recorded, and the recordings shall be preserved for three months.

evidence.quote: The bank shall ensure that there is a tape recording of the content / text of the calls made by recovery agents to the customers, and vice-versa.

rationale: The rule in force requires recording but sets no retention period. The Fourth Amendment (rbi-13665) requires six months, but only from 1 January 2027, after the snapshot; the clause will need revising then.
author: ai:claude

text: Complaints received through the Bank's official social media handles shall be acknowledged within four hours.
rationale: No corpus notification sets service timelines for complaints received through social media or chatbots (searched: social media / chatbot / virtual assistant near complaint or grievance).
author: ai:claude

text: Annual Customer Service Excellence awards for employees shall be decided by the Head of Human Resources.
rationale: Internal staff recognition; despite the customer-service wording no RBI regulation governs employee awards.
author: ai:claude

text: Borrowers shall be given the option to exit a digital loan during a cooling-off period of three days from disbursal, by paying the principal and the proportionate annual percentage rate without any penalty.

evidence.quote: The cooling off period shall be determined by the bank in terms of its credit policy, subject to the period so determined not being less than one day.

rationale: Three days exceeds the one-day minimum. The commercial-bank rule is in the Credit Facilities Directions; the 2025 Digital Lending Directions (rbi-12848) carry the same text and are acceptable.
author: ai:claude

text: The credit limit of a digital borrower may be increased automatically where the repayment record is satisfactory, after informing the borrower by SMS.

evidence.quote: A bank shall ensure that there is no automatic increase in credit limit unless an explicit request is received, evaluated and kept on record from the borrower for such increase.

rationale: Credit limits may not be raised automatically without an explicit, recorded request from the borrower; an SMS intimation does not suffice.
author: ai:claude

text: Digital loans may be disbursed to the account of the lending service provider for onward credit to the borrower.

evidence.quote: The bank shall ensure that in no case, disbursal is made to a third-party account, including the accounts of LSP, except as provided in this Chapter.

rationale: Disbursal to an LSP's account is prohibited.
author: ai:claude

text: Fees and charges that are not mentioned in the Key Facts Statement shall not be charged to the borrower.

evidence.quote: Any fees, charges, etc. which are not mentioned in the KFS, cannot be charged by the bank to the borrower at any stage during the term of the loan, without explicit consent of the borrower.

rationale: An absolute bar is stricter than the rule, which allows such charges only with the borrower's explicit consent.
author: ai:claude

text: If a complaint against the Bank or its lending service provider is not resolved within 30 days, the borrower may lodge a complaint under the Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme.

evidence.quote: or the borrower has not received any reply within 30 days of receipt of complaint by the bank, the said borrower can lodge a complaint over the Complaint Management System (CMS - https://cms.rbi.org.in/) portal

rationale: Escalation is also available when the complaint is rejected wholly or partly or the borrower is dissatisfied, and this must be conveyed to the borrower; the clause covers only non-resolution in 30 days (the 2022 Guidelines' wording, rbi-12382).
author: ai:claude

text: Before a recovery agent contacts a defaulting borrower, the particulars of the agent shall be communicated to the borrower by email or SMS.

evidence.quote: the particulars of such recovery agent authorised to approach the borrower for recovery shall be communicated to the borrower through email / SMS before the recovery agent contacts the borrower for recovery.

rationale: Matches para 9(6).
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank's digital lending application may access the borrower's contact list, with the borrower's explicit consent, for verifying references.

evidence.quote: In any case, the bank shall also ensure that DLA of the bank / LSP desist from accessing mobile phone resources like file and media, contact list, call logs, telephony functions, etc.

rationale: Digital lending apps must not access the contact list at all; consent does not make it permissible.
author: ai:claude

text: All data collected through the Bank's digital lending applications shall be stored only on servers located in India.

evidence.quote: Further, in case the data is processed outside India, the same shall be deleted from servers outside India and brought back to India within 24 hours of processing.

rationale: Storage in India is right, but data processed abroad must be deleted there and brought back within 24 hours; the clause omits it (the 2022 Guidelines had storage only).
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank may accept default loss guarantee arrangements from lending service providers on credit card portfolios sourced digitally, with cover not exceeding 5 per cent of the amount disbursed.

evidence.quote: A bank shall not enter into DLG arrangements for revolving credit facilities offered through digital lending channel and credit cards

rationale: DLG arrangements are not permitted for credit cards or digitally offered revolving credit, whatever the cap.
author: ai:claude

text: The Bank shall invoke a default loss guarantee within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the borrower makes good the dues earlier.

evidence.quote: A bank shall invoke DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the loan dues are made good by the borrower before that.

rationale: Matches para 27(1).
author: ai:claude

text: Machine-learning credit-scoring models used for digital loans shall undergo an independent bias audit every year.
rationale: No corpus notification addresses explainability or bias testing of AI/ML credit models (searched: bias / explainab / machine learning / artificial intelligence); AI is mentioned only as an optional KYC monitoring aid (rbi-13141 para 40) and in the regulatory sandbox framework.
author: ai:claude

text: Prizes for the Digital Lending team's quarterly internal hackathon shall be approved by the Head of Innovation.
rationale: Internal team event; no RBI regulation governs it.
author: ai:claude
